title: claude upgrade report mode prints the canon roster, not a diff, so a clean estate and a stale one look identical
body:
`intent claude upgrade` without `--apply` prints the canon ROSTER, not a diff. It names every file canon covers whether or not that file would change, so **an operator cannot tell "everything is already canonical" from "everything needs rewriting" -- the output is byte-identical in both states.**

**This is the second, independent cause behind issue 0110's consequence 2**, and it survives 0110's fix. 0110 said *"report mode lists `AGENTS.md` as would-write forever, so an operator can never see a clean canon state"* and attributed it to the renderer's blank-line runs. The renderer is fixed (`f02fb55f`, live in the published pair at `4479264f`) and report mode still names the file. It always would have: it never compared.

## Measured, on a project where nothing whatsoever would be written

A throwaway `intent init` under a decoy HOME, canon already applied, so every path is byte-identical to what the generator produces:

    $ intent claude upgrade --apply
    unchanged: .claude/settings.json
    unchanged: CLAUDE.md
    unchanged: AGENTS.md
    unchanged: .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent
    unchanged: .git/hooks/pre-commit
    ok: 0 written, 5 already canonical, 2 preserved, 0 held.

**`0 written, 5 already canonical`** -- there is nothing to do. And on the same project, immediately after:

    $ intent claude upgrade
    canon (dry run): would apply v3 canon to <project>
      .claude/settings.json
      CLAUDE.md
      AGENTS.md
      usage-rules.md (only if absent)
      .intent_critic.yml (only if absent)
      <project>/.git/hooks/pre-commit.intent (the gate shim)
      <project>/.git/hooks/pre-commit (chain block, region-edited)
    re-run with --apply to write.

Seven paths listed as *would apply* when the true answer is zero. Reproduced identically on Intent's own tree, where report mode names `CLAUDE.md` while `--apply` on the same tree reports `unchanged: CLAUDE.md`.

## Why it matters

**The two modes disagree about the same question and only one of them can be checked cheaply.** `--apply` computes the real answer as a side effect of doing the work; report mode exists precisely so an operator can ask *what would change* without writing, and it is the mode that cannot answer. So the safe, read-only path is the one that tells you least, and the only way to learn whether canon is clean is to run the writer.

**It is also the class this estate keeps meeting from new directions: an instrument whose output is the same whether or not the condition it reports on holds.** A census that cannot report that it is blind; `rc=0` with zero rows that cannot be told from an empty set (issue `0103`); `written:` that cannot be told from `changed:` (issue `0110`). Here it is a dry run that cannot be told from a no-op.

**The word `would` is doing the damage.** A roster headed *would apply v3 canon to* is a truthful list of what canon COVERS read as a list of what canon WOULD WRITE, and nothing in the output marks which reading is meant.

## Shape of a fix, not a design

`--apply` already computes the per-file verdict (`written` / `unchanged` / `preserved` / `held`) and already refrains from writing when nothing changed. Report mode should render that same verdict set with the writes suppressed, rather than enumerating the roster -- one computation, two renderings. Two paths answering *what would change* is the Highlander shape, and the copy that drifts is the one nobody exercises.

Found by intent-cc while verifying 0110 end to end through the published binary, 2026-08-28. Not chased; filed so 0110 is not read as closing all three of its stated consequences.
